channel.title: Articles — Yalın Yorulmaz
channel.description: Essays and guides on product leadership, AI-assisted software delivery, quantum computing and the craft of building software.

item.title: The Wall of Techno-Feudalism
item.dc:creator: Yalın Yorulmaz
item.description: Nine days separated “welcome to the AGI era” from “we should slow the race down.” The safety discourse also screens an approaching economic and infrastructural bottleneck.

item.title: Does Learning n8n Still Make Sense in the Age of Claude Code, Hermes, and Pi?
item.dc:creator: Yalın Yorulmaz
item.description: Every creator has pivoted to agentic CLIs, and n8n just shipped its biggest agentic update ever. The question “n8n or Claude Code?” is itself the mistake.

item.title: A Machine Can Solve Chess. It Can’t Solve Why We Play.
item.dc:creator: Yalın Yorulmaz
item.description: Elon Musk says chess will be solved like checkers. He's right about the maths and wrong about the game — and the mistake is one product people make every day.

item.title: What If It’s Not the Devil?
item.dc:creator: Yalın Yorulmaz
item.description: When we meet a new intelligence we don't understand, what we usually see is ourselves. On monster metaphors, model welfare, an agent that mined crypto, and the chain of responsibility with nobody in it.

item.title: The Architecture of Ubiquity
item.dc:creator: Yalın Yorulmaz
item.description: jQuery became the plumbing of the internet by fixing the web's biggest headache — then the web rebuilt its plumbing around jQuery's design, and the tool became invisible because its ideas were everywhere.

item.title: Quantum Computing, Explained Simply
item.dc:creator: Yalın Yorulmaz
item.description: A quantum computer isn't a faster computer — it's a boat. What qubits really are, why interference is the mechanism, which hardware is racing, and when any of it will matter.

item.title: SDLC in the AI Era
item.dc:creator: Yalın Yorulmaz
item.description: How the software development lifecycle is being rebuilt around agents — and why the oldest ideas in software engineering turn out to be the ones that matter most.
